note: These pages are for names that the direct line carries (or that the research files treat as a family under investigation) and that have no cluster of their own among the thirteen. A page for one of them is built entirely from people this archive already publishes: the numbered ancestors, the thirteen clusters and the relatives named beside them. Adding a name to this list adds a page and publishes nobody. That is the difference from the thirteen, whose every bearer in the tree is published: a name here lists only the people the archive already names, and says so.
match: A person belongs to a name when their surname field in the exported tree, lowercased, with apostrophes and quotation marks removed and cut at the first comma, bracket or parenthesis, equals one of the name's keys. Where the tree writes a title in place of a surname, the person is counted when their own name contains the surname. A person already in one of the thirteen clusters is never counted here, and a declared copy (the same person entered twice, ruled on in same-person.json) is never listed.
rule: A name is core when a direct-line ancestor carries it, or at least 8 published people carry it, or the archive's own research files (the work list, the search register, the open questions, the errands) treat it as a family under investigation. Published people are the numbered ancestors, the thirteen clusters and the relatives named beside them, minus declared copies. Core names are ranked direct line first, then published people, then research-file rows, then direct-line ancestors, and the twelve highest with no page of their own are given one.

pagesElsewhere._note: Names that have a page of their own that is not in families.json or this file. Used only to link a name where another family's page mentions it, and by tools/audit_family_lines.py. The spellings are the ones the archive's own namefold and spellings page group.

otherArchive.note: The Falco-side families. They are core by the direct-line test, but this archive's work list (item 19) sets the Australian and Italian side down deliberately, and the research on them is the Falco archive's. They are not treated here as families under investigation, so no line is offered for them here; the families index links each to its own page in the Falco archive.
